_schema: GOLEM v0.3 quarantined-vocabulary registry. Each record is a VocabEntry. status='quarantine' means the compiler path exists and is verified but the kind is NOT trusted: promotion to 'trusted' is a human act performed outside this file (there is deliberately no automated promotion mechanism).

vocab.frame_doc: Rounded box / prism. Axes: +x = creature's LEFT, +y = up, +z = forward; world units. Local axes equal world axes unless 'rot' is present. size = CORE half-extents along the part's local axes (NOT full widths). round (>= 0) is an additive OUTWARD fillet radius applied equally to every face, edge and corner, so the total half-extent along each axis is size + round and the compiled AABB is enlarged by round on every side. SDF (exact): let pl = R^T (p - center) (R = identity if no rot); q = |pl| - size; d = ||max(q,0)|| + min(max(q_x,q_y,q_z),0) - round. Mirror across x=0 sends center.x -> -center.x and, if oriented, the quaternion (w,x,y,z) -> (w,x,-y,-z). rot on a box is permitted (see the 'rot' entry); rot on a gencyl is forbidden.

Per-part orientation for blob and box ONLY. Schema: 'rot':[w,x,y,z], a unit quaternion in canonical double-cover form w >= 0. It is normalized and sign-canonicalized on read; if |q| differs far from 1 that is a reported violation (R-quat-nonunit) but the normalized quaternion is still used. Orientation is applied by isometry conjugation: d(p) = d_local(R^T (p - center)), where R = quat_to_matrix(q) is the local->world rotation. Exact for box; for blob the frozen scaled-space ellipsoid approximation is preserved unchanged inside the rotated frame. Mirror rule (across x=0): center.x -> -center.x and (w,x,y,z) -> (w,x,-y,-z); for box/blob this reflection is realized as the proper rotation R' = M R M with M = diag(-1,1,1), the improper factor being absorbed by the per-axis reflection symmetry of the box/ellipsoid local SDF, so the mirrored instance is the exact geometric reflection of the original. FENCE: rot on a gencyl is FORBIDDEN because spines already carry orientation; it is a reported violation (FENCE-rot-on-gencyl) and is NEVER applied -- a gencyl is always evaluated exactly as in v0.2.

Swept-superellipse cross-section for gencyl ONLY. Schema: 'profile': {'n': scalar-or-per-anchor list, exactly zero or one of 'aspect' and absolute 'depth': scalar-or-per-anchor list, 'roll': scalar-or-per-anchor degrees optional, 'offset': [u,v] or per-anchor pairs optional, 'up': [x,y,z] optional}; omission of both depth forms defaults aspect to 1. The cross-section is |u/width|^n + |v/depth|^n = 1 with width from radii, depth = width*aspect for the legacy relative form or the authored world-unit half-depth for the absolute form. n is checked against [2,12], all depths must be positive, aspect outside (0,1] is advisory, and per-anchor lists must match spine arity. Frame before roll: u = normalize(up x tangent), v = tangent x u; positive roll rotates the width axis toward v about the tangent. SDF is approximate: scaled radial superellipse distance follows linearly interpolated station parameters over each spine segment, interior station sections glue the local cover, and signed axial flat caps exist only at the whole-spine endpoints. Mirror across x=0 reflects the frame, negates roll, and negates the local width offset. FENCE: profile on blob/box is reported and ignored; rot on gencyl is reported and ignored.

Strictly opt-in post-extraction flesh detail. Schema at the creature or graph document root: 'surface_detail': {'kind':'curvature','amplitude': non-negative world distance, 'scale': positive world distance no larger than the extracted creature mesh diagonal}. The engine heat-diffuses the extracted mesh over the authored scale, projects the signed fine-to-coarse offset onto outward vertex normals, pushes convex crowns outward, creases concave mass boundaries inward, and clamps every realized offset by amplitude through a bounded response. Assembly rejects use on equipment and amplitudes above 0.9 times extracted-mesh pitch. Omission and zero amplitude are exact identities: no displacement report is emitted and compiled/exported geometry remains byte-identical. Face connectivity is never changed; export recomputes normals from displaced geometry.

Anatomy-facing generalized cylinder authored on body flesh as {'kind':'loft','sections':[...]} with at least two strictly increasing stations. Every section carries exactly finite station, positive half-width, positive absolute half-depth, exponent in [2,12], and finite roll degrees. The body owner lowers it directly into the existing gencyl field owner: spine points follow the bone axis, radii are widths, profile.depth carries absolute depths, profile.n carries exponents, profile.roll carries degrees, and profile.up is bone-local +y in world, making zero-roll width bone-local +x. This expresses keeled or deep chests, tucked waists, wedge skulls, and flat shins without a parallel geometry pipeline. Approximation bound: the field differs from an ideal continuous sweep by at most the Hausdorff distance between that sweep and the piecewise-linear spine and section-parameter interpolation declared by adjacent stations.

Ordered union operator carried by each incoming part or body flesh record. 'blend' is the existing polynomial smooth minimum and uses the selected blend radius; it remains the default when operator is absent. 'chamfer' uses a linear bevel union with that radius. 'crease' is exact hard min(a,b). Chamfer and crease avoid smooth-min bulge overshoot at joints; crease is pointwise identical to the primitive hard union. The operator belongs to the union edge formed when the part enters authored order, not to an isolated primitive.

Tier-two myology mass authored at top-level muscles. The minimal base form carries kind, id, origin, insertion, bulk, and definition. bulk is exactly one of {'relative':{'to':'origin'|'insertion'|'span','width':positive fraction,'depth':positive fraction}} or {'absolute':{'width':positive half-extent,'depth':positive half-extent}}. A relative origin or insertion part anchor uses that emitted part's full maximum cross-section girth; a bone or landmark anchor uses its host bone length; span uses solved anchor distance. definition is in [0,1]. The compiler derives a five-section fusiform profile with tendinous endpoints, shoulders, and a mid-span belly, then lowers it through the existing LoftSection and profiled gencyl owners. Detailed opt-in refinement replaces bulk and definition with legacy sections covering normalized span [0,1] and containing an interior belly wider and deeper than both tendinous endpoints. sections, bulk, and mirror_of are disjoint forms; relative and absolute are disjoint bulk units. Origin and insertion reuse the body relation selector grammar and must resolve to existing bone, part, or landmark constructed geometry; no myology-specific address syntax exists. mirror_of inherits and reflects the source derived or explicit profile after verifying the target anchors agree with sagittal reflection. blend, chamfer, and crease remain the existing incoming union-edge operators. Approximation bound: surface-distance error is bounded by the profiled gencyl piecewise-linear station interpolation over the resolved anchor span.
